## Gate 2.5 findings + architect recommendation
Gate 2.5 - Findings & Dispositions (model=deepseek-v4.1-flash sha=e67bf9a84642)
**Overall architect recommendation: APPROVE**
Findings: 6 (BLOCKER 0 / MAJOR 1 / MINOR 3 / NIT 2); dispositions: actioned 6; all blockers/majors actioned
status: PENDING | ACTIONED | ACCEPTED | DEFERRED | REJECTED | SCOPE

| # | Severity | Finding | Disposition | Response / resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MAJOR | none (prior MAJOR on regex narrowing and runbook divergence is resolved by this delta: `(`/`[`/`-`-prefixed forms now classify as `db_unavailable`, and the boundary excludes `_ . -` prefixes as the runbook implies). | ACTIONED | No action: reviewer explicitly recorded no major finding; separator/case tests added separately. evidence: go/edpsvc/main_test.go, go/edpdata/edpdata_test.go. |
| 2 | MINOR | The new boundary class `[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]` accepts *any* non-alphanumeric separator, so `foo/x509:`, `foo=x509:`, `foo"x509:`, `foo:x509:` now map to `db_unavailable` where they previously were `internal_error`; only `(`, `[`, space and `-` are pinned in tests, so the broadened acceptance set is untested in the positive direction for most separators (AC-1 classifier surface). | ACTIONED | Fixed in current HEAD; separator and uppercase cases pinned. evidence: go/edpsvc/main_test.go, go/edpdata/edpdata_test.go. |
| 3 | MINOR | No negative test for the widened class: e.g. an embedded token in unrelated error text preceded by punctuation (e.g. `result/x509: ...` from a non-cert source) is now classified `db_unavailable`, which can mask genuine `internal_error` signals; add at least one adversarial case documenting this trade-off. | ACTIONED | Fixed in current HEAD; separator and uppercase cases pinned. evidence: go/edpsvc/main_test.go, go/edpdata/edpdata_test.go. |
| 4 | MINOR | Negation is ASCII-only: a Unicode letter preceding the token (e.g. `éx509:`) is treated as a boundary and maps to `db_unavailable` despite being part of a word; low risk but worth a one-line rationale or explicit test. | ACTIONED | Fixed in current HEAD; separator and uppercase cases pinned. evidence: go/edpsvc/main_test.go, go/edpdata/edpdata_test.go. |
| 5 | NIT | Case sensitivity is unchanged (`X509:` uppercase still yields `internal_error`); since the regex is being reworked in this delta, add a comment or case so the intended case posture is documented rather than incidental. | ACTIONED | Fixed in current HEAD; separator and uppercase cases pinned. evidence: go/edpsvc/main_test.go, go/edpdata/edpdata_test.go. |
| 6 | NIT | Add a one-line comment on the boundary class rationale (why `.`/`_`/`-` are treated as word-continuations) — the rule is non-obvious and future edits are likely. | ACTIONED | Fixed in current HEAD; separator and uppercase cases pinned. evidence: go/edpsvc/main_test.go, go/edpdata/edpdata_test.go. |

--- SUMMARY (review) ---
  Delta is tightly scoped, correct in intent, and fixes the prior wrapped-x509 misclassification while preserving the bounded reason set; no integrity, security, tenant, migration or language-rule issues.
  Residual risk is limited to classifier false-positives from the intentionally broad separator class, which is currently only partially pinned by tests.
  Recommend merge after adding one or two boundary tests/comments; no blockers.
